walkthroughs.body_html:
Communicating Visual Arts — a core area of Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Communicating Visual Arts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Communicating Visual Arts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose triadic sign distinguishes icon, index and symbol?
options: Saussure
Peirce
Eco
Hjelmslev

mcqs.q: Whose 1964 Rhetoric of the Image analysed Panzani's pasta ad?
options: Barthes
Metz
Lyotard
Bourdieu

mcqs.q: What is the rule of thirds?
options: Designers must follow strict government forms.
A guideline placing key elements along lines or intersections of a 3x3 grid.
Using exactly three colours.
A strict mathematical rule that must never be broken.

mcqs.q: Why is preserving white in watercolour important?
options: White comes from the paper showing through - there is no true white pigment in traditional watercolour.
Because white is the most expensive colour.
Using exactly three colours.
You can simply paint white over other colours later.
Decoration is the most important aspect of design.
An object's design should be determined by its purpose.
Because white is the most expensive colour.
Designers must follow strict government forms.
